column1: # The demo video's narration (about two minutes): <segment><TAB><what Marin says>. Segments match flotilla-90s-build.py.
# For someone who has never heard of Flotilla: the developer who built it, showing what it does, in order. The Mac
# and the cloud first; then the iPhone.
# The name never starts a sentence: Marin says "Flotillo" there. The idle and ask lines are Joseph's wording
# (2026-11-02): the VMs are why agents keep working with the laptop shut. The last line is his (draft 4 notes).

column2: Run four coding agents on one laptop and they fight over its files and ports. In Flotilla, each one works alone in its own cloud VM.
For a new thread, I type the task and pick Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode.
It gets a fresh VM with my repo already set up, and it's working in seconds.
The app runs in that VM too, and Preview opens it in my browser.
Make public gives anyone the link, for an hour or until I stop it.
The pull request appears on the thread with its checks. One failed, so I asked for the missing changelog line.
Once they pass, I hold the button down to merge.
Agents can hand work to each other. Here Opus asked Codex and Fable to review its code, then fixed what they found.
The VMs run on boat.dev, so they keep working with my laptop shut. When one sits idle it stops, and it wakes the moment I send.
I can also send prompts on a schedule, like a dependency check every weekday at nine.
Other assistants can use Flotilla as well. Here Claude Code starts a thread and reads its answer. Assistants in other clouds, like Grok Bot, can connect too.
Here's Flotilla on my iPhone, with the same threads, live.
When an agent asks me a question, I can answer from the Mac or the phone.
All the features of the desktop app, in your pocket.
It's free and open source, at useflotilla.com.
